clue.text: Random test for acne

parts.note: an unannounced inspection, read literally as an examination of the skin for pimples

explanation.surface: A doctor proposes screening patients for acne at random.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for a surprise inspection also reads as a check for spots, which is what acne produces.
explanation.definitionFit: An unannounced inspection carried out on a sample is the everyday name for a random test.

clue.text: Bow out of a quarrel with coppers

parts.note: coppers are pennies, abbreviated P
a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: Someone bows out of a dispute involving the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests police, but here it means small coins, pence, giving P.
explanation.definitionFit: The bow is the front end of a ship, also called its prow.

clue.text: Embroidery frame used by a drummer

definitions.meaning: a circular hoop that holds fabric taut for stitching
a drum, as played by a drummer

explanation.surface: A drummer borrows a needlework hoop.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a round needlework hoop and, from French, a drum.

clue.text: Fish is what a fiance should buy

definitions.meaning: split as two words, the ring for his bride-to-be

explanation.surface: A joke that a fish is what an engaged man must purchase.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer three letters in and it says what a man buys his fiancée: the ring for her.
explanation.definitionFit: A herring is a common North Atlantic food fish.

clue.text: Firm and popular currency

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A stable, widely accepted money.
explanation.definitionFit: Coins are metal money, part of a country's currency.

clue.text: Discounting one reason for a flat battery

definitions.text: one reason for a flat battery
definitions.meaning: not feeding enough current into a battery

explanation.surface: A shop discounting stock is compared with a battery left flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking a lower price than due is a form of discounting; a battery given too little current goes flat.

clue.text: Minced meat in gravies? Not likely!

definitions.text: Minced meat in gravies? Not likely!

indicators.note: minced meat is chopped up, so these letters are chopped and reassembled

explanation.surface: A diner refuses minced meat in gravy outright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minced' rearranges MEAT IN GRAVIES; the whole clue also describes the answer, a creed refusing meat in any form.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abstains from eating animal flesh would say 'not likely' to any mince in gravy.

clue.text: Long ago he blew the whistle daily

parts.note: a man who blows the whistle reports wrongdoing, an informer
the Times is a daily newspaper

explanation.surface: A whistleblower exposed a daily paper long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in days gone by, an idiom for long ago.

clue.text: Only Tories are perfect

parts.note: just means only
Tories are the political right

explanation.surface: A partisan claim that only Conservatives are flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: Tories are Britain's Conservative Party, on the political right.
explanation.definitionFit: Exactly as it should be, an idiom for perfect.

clue.text: Righteous suffering? You amaze me!

parts.note: good means virtuous or righteous
grief is suffering

explanation.surface: An exclamation at the idea that virtue brings suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of surprise or dismay, the same feeling as 'you amaze me'.

clue.text: Accustomed to being manipulated

definitions.meaning: familiar with, as in being in the habit of something

explanation.surface: Someone has grown accustomed to being manipulated.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both habituated (followed by 'to') and exploited by another.

clue.text: Drop by when Dad's not out

parts.note: pop is a familiar name for father
not out means in

explanation.surface: Visit when your father is at home.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay a short casual visit is to drop by.

clue.text: I object to Maureen delivering a note

parts.note: ME is the object form of I
Mo is short for the name Maureen

explanation.surface: A protester objects to Maureen handing over a message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I object' is grammar: the objective case of I is ME, not a protest.
explanation.definitionFit: A short written message at work is a note.

clue.text: A Hebrew

parts.note: read as the letter A in the Hebrew alphabet, not a Hebrew person

explanation.surface: A Jewish person is mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A Hebrew' looks like a person, but means the Hebrew letter corresponding to A, the first of its alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: The first letter of the Hebrew alphabet corresponds to our A.

clue.text: Square-bashing is meant to bore

explanation.surface: Parade-ground practice is designed to be dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square-bashing' is British slang for marching practice on a parade ground; 'bore' is the verb, not dullness.
explanation.definitionFit: Marching practice is military training, and a tool that bores holes is the same word.

clue.text: Problem for a trout fisherman

definitions.meaning: one who catches trout by stroking them by hand

explanation.walkthrough: Poachers catch trout by 'tickling' them by hand; a knotty problem is also a word for this.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricky puzzle is a teaser, and someone who catches fish by stroking them is one too.

clue.text: Crown used by Liza Minelli's mother

definitions.meaning: a wreath worn on the head
Judy, the film star of The Wizard of Oz

explanation.surface: A tiara worn by a Hollywood star's mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A wreath of flowers worn as a crown shares its name with the singer Judy, mother of Liza Minnelli.

clue.text: Having trouble finding where the pus is

explanation.surface: Struggling to locate an infection.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in difficulties is the idiom, and pus collects within a pimple.

clue.text: Corresponds with thickheaded friends

parts.note: the head of the word thick is its first letter T
allies are friends

explanation.surface: Someone writes letters to dim-witted friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thickheaded' looks like stupid, but means the head (first letter) of 'thick'.
explanation.definitionFit: When two accounts match they agree, so one tallies with the other.

clue.text: Tommy drops iodine into lead-and-tin alloy

indicators.note: into says where the dropped iodine ends up, within the alloy

parts.note: solder is a lead and tin alloy
a drop of iodine, chemical symbol I, is what is let fall

explanation.surface: A man spills iodine into a metal mix.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy is a nickname for a British private soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Tommy Atkins was the generic name for a British private, an infantryman.

clue.text: Muslim soldier given unusual care in the sickbay

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the sickbay

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a sickbay

indicators.note: unusual means not in the usual form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Muslim fighter gets odd treatment in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges 'care', and 'in' puts the result inside SAN; SAN, short for sanatorium, is a school or barracks sickbay.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval Christians called a Muslim warrior of the Crusades by this name.

clue.text: Elephantine girl initially put in the shade

parts.note: a hue is a shade of colour

indicators.note: initially means the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A large girl is overshadowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something as big as an elephant is enormous.

clue.text: Very light food left inside

parts.note: fare is food

explanation.surface: A diet meal with leftovers inside.
explanation.walkthrough: A Very light is a signal flare fired from a pistol, named after its inventor Very; it is not 'very' meaning extremely.
explanation.definitionFit: A coloured signal fired from a pistol is a pyrotechnic distress light.

clue.text: Unit comprised 100 in the past

indicators.note: comprised means contained, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: one is a unit
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A military unit used to be a hundred strong.
explanation.definitionFit: Formerly, at some earlier time, means in the past.

clue.text: She cleans and makes tea

explanation.surface: A housekeeper cleans and brews tea.
explanation.walkthrough: A char (charwoman) is a British cleaner; 'char' is also British slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A charwoman is a daily cleaner, and the same short word is old slang for a cuppa.

clue.text: Nothing more than two notes

parts.note: me is the third note of the sol-fa scale
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A tune of merely two notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Merely, a mere pittance, means no more than.

clue.text: I cannot see her organisation growing

indicators.note: organisation means putting into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone cannot see her company expanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming larger or more numerous is the idiom for growing.

clue.text: Reigning queen wins the MC

parts.note: present means current, as with a reigning monarch
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: The current queen beats the master of ceremonies.
explanation.definitionFit: An MC is a host who introduces a show.
